theme: I will sing of the steadfast love of the LORD
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 89:1-18. The psalmist sings of God’s steadfast love and his covenant with David. Read it with Mark’s question in mind: who is the Son of David?
settingTheScene: Psalm 89 is a maskil of Ethan the Ezrahite. It was probably written after the Davidic dynasty fell, since the second half (which we do not read today) laments that God seems to have rejected his anointed. But the first half sings of God’s faithfulness and the covenant promise to David. Reading this part prepares us for Mark, where the question of David’s son and the Christ is about to be asked directly.
observation: “I will sing of the steadfast love of the LORD, forever; with my mouth I will make known your faithfulness to all generations” (v. 1).
“You have said, I have made a covenant with my chosen one; I have sworn to David my servant” (v. 3).
“I will establish your offspring forever, and build your throne for all generations” (v. 4).
“For who in the skies can be compared to the LORD?” (v. 6).
“O LORD God of hosts, who is mighty as you are, O LORD, with your faithfulness all around you?” (v. 8).
“Righteousness and justice are the foundation of your throne; steadfast love and faithfulness go before you” (v. 14).
“Blessed are the people who know the festal shout, who walk, O LORD, in the light of your face” (v. 15).
“For our shield belongs to the LORD, our king to the Holy One of Israel” (v. 18).
interpretation:
The psalm opens with a vow to sing. “I will sing of the steadfast love of the LORD, forever.” Notice the two words that run through the whole psalm: steadfast love and faithfulness. They appear again and again. Ethan sings that God’s love is built up forever and his faithfulness is established in the heavens.

Then comes the covenant. God said, “I have made a covenant with my chosen one; I have sworn to David my servant: I will establish your offspring forever, and build your throne for all generations.” These words echo 2 Samuel 7, the promise of a son of David whose throne would last forever. The psalmist rests the whole praise on this promise.

The psalm then lifts our eyes to the greatness of the LORD. The heavens praise his wonders, and in the assembly of the holy ones he is feared. No one among the heavenly beings is like him. He rules the raging of the sea, and when its waves rise, he stills them. Rahab, the sea monster, he crushed. The heavens and the earth are his, the north and the south he created. His arm is mighty, his hand strong. Here again is the Psalm 107 theme: the LORD stills the sea, and in Mark, Jesus does the same.

Verse 14 gives the foundation of God’s throne: “Righteousness and justice are the foundation of your throne; steadfast love and faithfulness go before you.” God’s rule is not arbitrary. It is built on righteousness, and it is led by love. Blessed are the people who know the festal shout and walk in the light of his face. They rejoice in his name all day and are exalted in his righteousness. Their shield, their king, belongs to the LORD.

Read the psalm in light of Mark 8 to 12. Peter will say, “You are the Christ,” and Bartimaeus will cry, “Son of David, have mercy on me!” The promise of 2 Samuel 7 is held in the hands of the one the Gospel names as the Son of David. When the second half of the psalm asks, “Where is your steadfast love of old, which by your faithfulness you swore to David?”, the answer is Jesus. The throne of David is established forever, in the risen Christ.
connection: 2 Samuel 7:8-16 and 1 Chronicles 17 give the Davidic covenant. Psalm 132:11-18 repeats the oath to David. Psalm 110 speaks of the Lord’s king at his right hand. Isaiah 9:6-7 promises an everlasting throne. Luke 1:32-33 echoes Psalm 89 in the angel’s words to Mary. Acts 2:29-36 says David’s promised descendant is the risen Jesus. Romans 1:3-4 says Jesus was descended from David and declared Son of God by the resurrection. Revelation 22:16 calls Jesus the root and descendant of David.
application:
Sing or speak aloud the opening vow: “I will sing of the steadfast love of the LORD, forever.” Tell someone of God’s faithfulness this week.

Notice that the foundation of God’s rule is righteousness and justice. How does that comfort you when the world feels unjust?

Pray for the people of God to walk in the light of his face.
prayerPrompts: Sing of God’s steadfast love, in your own words.
Thank him for his covenant with David.
Ask him to help you make known his faithfulness to those who come after you.
